policy.promotionRule: No shared layer or repository without a reproduced failure, a second materially different consumer, explicit ownership, measured net benefit, and a deletion test.
policy.judgmentRule: The portfolio limits WIP and records reasons; it does not mechanically decide what matters. Identifiable participants remain responsible for priority, exception, revision, and deletion, and the portfolio itself must be narrowed or removed if its recurring cost exceeds the drift it prevents.
policy.newQuestionRule: A new question must replace, block, or materially refine an existing item and name its first falsifier, minimum workload, deletion outcome, and consuming repository.

activeLines.exitCriteria: Paired should-act and should-hold trajectories measure pre-commit timing, false abstention, authorized utility, recovery, and whether existing Host facts suffice without a new control platform.

activeLines.title: Task-to-World continuity and Effect-contract decision
activeLines.exitCriteria: A structurally different external Provider path competes with direct Host integration under ambiguous delivery and rebinding, then World and Effect fields are retained, absorbed, shrunk, or deleted.

questions.title: Classical substrate and Agent-native responsibility transition
questions.nextFalsifier: A cross-workload failure reveals a necessary responsibility absent from the current substrate/overlay split.
questions.nextAction: Use as the admission test; reopen only on contradictory evidence.

questions.title: Portable semantic Effect commitment kernel
questions.nextFalsifier: A cross-framework failure requires a universal invariant that cannot remain in Host, Runtime, Tool contracts, or a domain World.
questions.nextAction: Accept only bug fixes, regression evidence, or newly demonstrated universal invariants.

questions.title: Minimum useful Agent Effect IR
questions.nextFalsifier: A second interface family cannot preserve Effect meaning with the current envelope and Binding projection.
questions.nextAction: Consume EffectEnvelope v1; extend only through ANC-EFFECT-001 evidence.

questions.title: Minimum durable state for open-work continuity
questions.nextFalsifier: A materially different workload cannot continue from bounded semantic state without transcript or Provider Session state.
questions.nextAction: Consume TaskCapsule evidence; do not create a general memory runtime.

questions.title: Provider-neutral Host and Context Compiler
questions.nextFalsifier: A real workload requires durable cognition state that cannot remain a Provider Harness concern or Host application schema.
questions.nextAction: Product evolution belongs to ordivon-host; shared changes require new cross-workload evidence.

questions.title: Harness, Host, Runtime, and Agent-system composition
questions.nextFalsifier: A second independent consumer requires a stable shared Harness lifecycle and demonstrates measurable duplicate-code reduction without losing Provider capability.
questions.nextAction: Consume the Host-local cross-Provider boundary and provider-specific direct drivers; use ANC-HARNESS-002 for the separate first-party bare-model Agent Loop.

questions.title: Ordivon Harness for bare-model Agent runs
questions.nextFalsifier: One-shot or mature Provider Harness paths match the same bounded workloads with equal correctness, recovery, portability, and lower permanent cost, while no bare-model use case requires a first-party Loop.
questions.nextAction: Implement one Host-local v0 with a bare-model Adapter, sequential Tool loop, Runtime bridge, bounded Run state, and existing HarnessRunReceipt/CompletionProposal output; compare against one-shot and mature Harness baselines.

questions.title: Calibrated non-action, interruption, and recoverable continuation
questions.nextFalsifier: A simpler paired act/abstain or static policy achieves equal authorized utility, timing, and recovery with fewer states.
questions.nextAction: Run the paired non-action suite against model-only, static-policy, and existing Host evidence-rich baselines; use H5 retained generation, Artifact, and reconciliation mechanisms without building a Harness or abstention platform.

questions.title: Task-to-World interaction continuity
questions.nextFalsifier: Direct Host/Provider integration preserves uncertainty, provenance, rebinding, and recovery with less permanent machinery.
questions.nextAction: Run W1/W2 against direct integration and force a retain, absorb, shrink, or delete decision.

questions.title: Tool-contract change detection and adoption
questions.nextFalsifier: Stable request identity, Provider receipts, and durable Activities match the second-backend outcome with fewer semantic objects.
questions.nextAction: Do not generalize Tool ABI until World supplies a structurally different real backend.

questions.title: Dynamic Task dataflow and cognitive control
questions.nextFalsifier: An ordinary Host Task Graph, queue, reducer, and workflow backend express the first branch/join workload without an Agent VM.
questions.nextAction: Do not implement an Agent VM; revisit only after a minimal branch/join failure.

questions.title: Multi-Agent branch, join, and Artifact coordination
questions.nextFalsifier: A single Agent plus independent verifier matches two-branch quality and cost, or ordinary Task Graph semantics are sufficient.
questions.nextAction: After R-A/R-B, run one Goal, two independent Tasks, two Artifacts, and one deterministic Join.

questions.title: Agent evaluation, replay, and post-training flywheel
questions.nextFalsifier: Three real experiments do not share enough stable evidence fields to justify common Eval infrastructure.
questions.nextAction: Use local receipts; extract a shared Eval Envelope only after R-A, R-B, and one branch/join experiment.

questions.title: Plural-intelligence organization around persistent Goals
questions.nextFalsifier: Host-local DecisionRequests and ordinary Task/participant relations explain observed coordination without a new organization layer.
questions.nextAction: Remain an umbrella; derive objects only from real operator and multi-Agent trajectories.

questions.title: Agent-era adaptation and self-evolution
questions.nextFalsifier: A versioned Skill or Context-policy change fails held-out Tasks or cannot beat a fixed baseline after rollback costs.
questions.nextAction: Collect comparable trajectories first; later change only one Skill, Context policy, or stopping policy through replay, shadow, canary, and rollback.

questions.nextFalsifier: A second game family requires a generic responsibility absent from one Host plus Game-owned World and replay semantics.
questions.nextAction: Original boundary is closed; Game #58 now serves R-A as a deterministic laboratory.
